| Newer major/track exists (uncounted) | no |

## Verdict: `do-now`

v2026.8.2 explicitly updates the managed Sharp dependency to fix "vulnerabilities in image decoding," which is a stated security fix, and v2026.9.1 adds further hardening around ingress, token, and secret-redaction boundaries. On top of that, v2026.8.1 ships two breaking migrations (removal of the bundled OpenProse plugin and the codex/openai-codex to openai model-ref migration) that require `openclaw doctor --fix` to complete, so this isn't a drop-in patch release.

## What it will take

Back up configuration and state first, then run the update followed by `openclaw doctor --fix` to complete the OpenProse and OpenAI route migrations, and restart/recreate the Gateway container; the notes also warn that a failed automatic update should be diagnosed before retrying.

## Source

Raw release notes this verdict was drawn from: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.9.1

| Releases behind | 5 |
| Minor boundary crossed | True |
| Newer major/track exists (uncounted) | no |

## Verdict: `do-now`

29.6.2 fixes five CVEs in BuildKit (command injection via Git checkout, /tmp deletion, destination directory validation bypass, and more), and 29.7.0 fixes CVE-2026-17106 in go-archive, so the notes explicitly flag real security content. Later releases also fix several regressions introduced in 29.7.0 itself (image pull failures on certain images and older kernels), so jumping straight to 29.8.0 avoids landing on a broken intermediate. Nothing in the notes describes a breaking config or API change requiring migration.

## What it will take

Nothing beyond the normal update process - a daemon restart, which will briefly stop and recreate running containers. One optional config tweak: if you relied on unlimited concurrent image pulls/pushes, set "max-concurrent-downloads" and "max-concurrent-uploads" to 0 to preserve the old behavior.

## Source
